s4.p1: Instance properties are _encapsulated_ within the instance
s4.p2: For example, the instance **⟦f2⟧** acts as a ‘capsule’ in which the properties **⟦f3⟧**, **⟦f4⟧** and **⟦f5⟧**  are separated from the same properties of other instances
s4.p3: It is possible to create an object **⟦f6⟧** with the same set of properties, but with different values for those properties:
s4.p4: The instances **⟦f2⟧** and **⟦f6⟧** have the same set of properties (the property names are the same)
s4.p5: However, the values of these properties differ in each instance
s4.p6: Therefore, **_an instance’s own properties are the properties encapsulated within that instance_**
s4.p7: ^^The properties  **_⟦f3⟧_**,  **_⟦f4⟧_**  and  **_⟦f5⟧_**  are **own** properties of the instances  **⟦f2⟧**  and  ** ⟦f6⟧** because their values are localised within the ‘capsule’ under the instance’s name )^^

s7.p1: It’s time to get to grips with what a constructor actually is
s7.p2: ![ico-25 warn] It is a function (_which means you can hide something inside it_)
s7.p3: ![ico-25 warn] For it to act as a **constructor**, you must prefix its name with the keyword **⟦f14⟧** when calling it; in this case:
s7.p4: ![ico-20 green-ok] it does not require the ⟦f15⟧ statement, but it will return an **instance** of the object
s7.p5: ![ico-20 green-ok] inside it, **⟦f16⟧** will refer not to the _global object_, but to the returned **instance**
s7.p6: ![ico-20 green-ok] all variables and functions declared within it will be _encapsulated_ in the created **instance** (_i.e. they will be the instance’s own properties and methods_)
s7.p7: ![ico-20 green-ok] it will have a property **⟦f12⟧** (_which only functions have_)
s7.p8: ![ico-20 green-ok] Whatever we place in the property **⟦f12⟧** will be _inherited_ by all instances
s7.p9: ![ico-25 warn] It is customary for constructor names to begin with a capital letter
s7.p10: Let’s print the instance **obj** to the console:
s7.p11: • We have created an empty object of the **Sample** class ^^(more precisely, we have created an instance of the object)^^
s7.p12: • It has no properties of its own ^^(because nothing has been declared in the constructor)^^
s7.p13: • It has a _prototype chain_ – these are properties nested one within the other  **⟦f8⟧**
s7.p14: • The first ‘link’ in the prototype chain is a reference to the property **⟦f12⟧** of the **Sample** constructor function
s7.p15: • The property **⟦f12⟧** of the constructor function **Sample** is an object
s7.p16: • This means that it also has a property **⟦f8⟧**
s7.p17: • This is the nested property **⟦f8⟧** – the next ‘link’ in the prototype chain
s7.p19: We can add properties to **⟦f12⟧** of the **Sample** constructor
s7.p20: If we now print the instance **obj** to the console, we will find a new enumerable property **_⟦f17⟧_** (_inherited method_) in its **⟦f8⟧** property
s7.p22: and we’ll find that the **obj** instance now has a new _own enumerable_ property **name**
s7.p23: ![ico-20 warn] When accessing a property, it is first searched for amongst the instance’s own properties; if not found, the search continues amongst the prototype’s properties, and so on, until the prototype chain ends
s7.p24: ![ico-25 pin] The constructor allows you to create instances of objects that have not only public but also private properties and methods
s8.p1: A constructor is a function; it follows, therefore, that a constructor can be used to ‘hide’ variables and functions
s8.p2: Where can they be hidden? – Within an instance created using that constructor
s8.p3: As we already know, a constructor creates **_its own_** properties and methods for instances by declaring variables and functions
s8.p4: ![ico-25 pin] All properties declared in the constructor with the keyword  **⟦f16⟧** will be **_public_**
s8.p5: ![ico-25 pin] All properties declared in the constructor using the keyword  **⟦f18⟧** or **⟦f19⟧** will be **_private_**
s8.p6: An instance’s public properties and methods are always accessible from the external environment
s8.p8: ^^When calling a method, you must also add round brackets after its name^^
s8.p9: An instance’s private properties (and methods) are not accessible from outside
s8.p10: They are not displayed in the console when the object is printed
s8.p11: In this example, **_⟦f20⟧_** and **_⟦f21⟧_** are **_private_** properties of the instance **⟦f22⟧**
s8.p12: **_⟦f23⟧_**, **_⟦f24⟧_** and **_⟦f25⟧_** are **_public_** properties of the instance **⟦f22⟧**
s8.p13: In the public methods of the instance (**_⟦f25⟧_**),  **⟦f16⟧**  will be a reference to the instance (**⟦f22⟧**)
s8.p14: ![ico-20 warn] In the instance’s private methods (**_⟦f21⟧_**), the call context will be the *global object* **⟦f26⟧**
s8.p15: (i.e. within the method **_⟦f21⟧_** ** ⟦f16⟧**  will be a reference to the object **⟦f26⟧**)
s8.p16: ^^The constructor **⟦f27⟧**  creates an object with private properties  **⟦f28⟧**,  **⟦f29⟧** and **⟦f30⟧**^^
s8.p17: ^^We use it to create an instance of **myCase**^^
s8.p18: ^^When creating the instance, we pass it the key phrase to access the contents of the handbag: ‘_it’s me, your mistress_’^^
s8.p19: ^^As the properties **⟦f28⟧**, **⟦f29⟧** and **⟦f30⟧** are private, “the handbag is locked”^^
s8.p20: ^^Outsiders have no access to its contents^^
s8.p21: ^^The public property **⟦f31⟧** initially has the value  **⟦f13⟧**^^
s8.p22: ^^That’s all you can see in the closed handbag^^
s8.p23: ^^If the owner of the bag agrees to show its contents, these will be placed in the public property **⟦f31⟧** for viewing^^
s8.p24: ^^The function **⟦f32⟧** for accessing the money (the private property **⟦f28⟧**) is also private, as no one other than the owner should be able to take money from the bag^^
s8.p28: ^^When a payment is made using the public method **payment**^^
s8.p29: ^^A key phrase is requested, checked against the one set when the instance was created, and if the values match, the private method **⟦f33⟧** is called, which decrements the private property ** ⟦f28⟧** by the amount of the payment,  whereupon  the public method **⟦f34⟧** returns the withdrawn amount with a clear conscience^^
s8.p30: ^^If an incorrect passphrase is entered, the request will be rejected and ![ico-20 err]^^ will be returned
s8.p31: ^^In the event of a customs inspection, the public method **rummage()** is called^^
s8.p32: ^^which ‘displays’ the contents of the handbag (placing them in the public property **⟦f31⟧**)^^
s8.p33: ^^Now customs officers can view the contents:^^
s8.p34: Thus, private and public properties and methods are placed within a ‘capsule’ – an object (instance)
s8.p36: The names of properties and methods inside the ‘capsule’ belong to the object’s namespace
s8.p37: We have aggregated under a single name (the object’s name) the entire set of variables and functions that define and modify its (the object’s) state
